Coverage Indications, Limitations and/or Medical Necessity
Magnetic resonance imaging of the lumbar spine is considered reasonable and
necessary when all of the following criteria are documented in the medical record.

The beneficiary has low back pain persisting for at least six weeks, with the
onset date recorded in the medical record by the ordering practitioner.

The beneficiary has undergone conservative management for at least four weeks
within the preceding six months. Conservative management includes supervised
physical therapy, analgesic or anti-inflammatory medication where not
contraindicated, or activity modification.

The beneficiary has documented neurological findings on physical examination,
including but not limited to radicular pain in a dermatomal distribution, motor
weakness, sensory deficit, or reflex asymmetry.

Where the presentation includes suspected malignancy, infection, or cauda equina
syndrome, the duration requirement above does not apply and imaging is considered
reasonable and necessary without delay.

Limitations
Magnetic resonance imaging of the lumbar spine is not covered when the record
documents an equivalent lumbar imaging study within the preceding sixty days
without a documented clinically significant interval change.

Documentation Requirements
The medical record must contain the symptom onset date, the conservative
management record with dates and modality, and the neurological examination
findings.

Revision History
R2 effective 2022-06-01. Neurological examination findings added as an explicit
requirement.
